name: The Glass Nebula

stars.name: Lampwright
stars.notes: A ferociously bright young blue star still embedded in the reflection nebula of its own nursery; its light scatters off the surrounding dust into sheets of silver and pale green that give the system its name.

planets.name: Kilnlight
planets.notes: A scorched inner rock bathed in hard ultraviolet; probes last minutes, and their final transmissions are prized by exactly one kind of collector.

planets.name: Vitrine
planets.notes: An airless world of glass-smooth obsidian plains that mirror the nebula overhead; the surface reflects the sky so perfectly that landings are flown by instrument alone.

planets.name: Silvergarden
planets.notes: A frozen moon-world whose crystalline plains catch the scattered light; the site of the nebula's only permanent outpost, a combined research platform and artists' residency.

stations.name: Prism Station
stations.notes: A stellar physics platform studying the nebula's light-scattering geometry; half its berths are leased to the Residency, which fills them with sculptors, composers, and one very patient cook.

stations.name: The Quiet Gallery
stations.notes: A small habitat in Vitrine's shadow where resident artists work in the mirrored dark; visits are by invitation, and invitations are rarely declined twice.

faction_control.notes: Chartered as a natural monument under joint research-cultural administration: no mining, no mass tourism, no permanent settlement beyond the two stations. The charter has held for sixty years because nobody has ever wanted anything here except to look.

history: The system was charted as a navigation hazard, not a destination: the nebula's dust shrouds it from most approaches and swallows unshielded sensors whole.
The Glassward Charter was written after the first survey images circulated; within a decade, three governments that had never agreed on anything ratified protection for a view.

Nine years ago a chartered freighter lost shielding inside the nebula and drifted for eleven days before rescue; its crew survived, and the captain's log of the light is read aloud at Prism Station every year.
description: There is no sky here in any ordinary sense. The young blue star sits at the heart of its own birth-cloud, and its furious light turns the surrounding dust into walls of silver, green, and pearl that stretch farther than the eye can follow. Three small worlds turn inside this lantern: a scorched stone, a black mirror-plain that doubles the heavens, and a frozen garden where the light comes down like slow rain.

Almost no one lives here, and everyone who does was chosen. A hundred and eighty researchers at Prism Station take apart the physics of the glow, while twenty-five residents at the Quiet Gallery attempt the impossible job of answering it in paint, sound, and glass. Traffic is a supply run a month and the occasional invited guest; the charter forbids everything louder than wonder.

Yet the place keeps its own counsel. The nebula's sheets of light drift and fold in patterns that repeat on no schedule instruments can find, though several residents swear they have seen the same figure return, years apart, in the same quarter of the sky. The physicists log it as persistence of structure. The artists log it as a subject. And the captain of the lost freighter wrote, on her eleventh day adrift, that she had stopped being sure which side of the glass she was on.
